newsitem.title: USA: Army reports 4,000 sexual harassment complaints.
newsitem.headline: Army reports 4,000 sexual harassment complaints.

text.p: More than 4,000 calls have been received at an Army hotline set up to investigate sexual harassment complaints from female trainees at bases across the country, Secretary of the Army Togo West Jr. said Sunday.
The hotline was set up after allegations of sexual harassment broke out at a training facility in Maryland in early November.

West said on the CBS "Face the Nation" programme about 550 of the calls were leads they intended to follow up. He said 74 percent of the calls involved other places than the Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland where 20 people have been suspended from their duties pending an investigation into allegations of sexual harassment.
"At the moment we're not clear on where we will eventually get all our reports from. We are looking at all of our training bases," he said.
He said the Army was concerned about whether sexual harassment at its bases was widespread.
